markdown:
## Bottom line
**Suggests InSitu (57%)** · Ambiguous: Benign vs InSitu · Careful review
Benign holds 39% and sits in the 90% conformal set; invasive probability is 2% [F1].

## Confidence
| Signal | Value | Reading |
|---|---|---|
| Top probabilities | InSitu 57%, Benign 39%, Normal 2%, Invasive 2% | Two classes compete |
| Conformal set | Benign, InSitu at α=0.1 | Cannot separate the two |
| Reliability / OOD | 0.96 / OOD percentile 1.0 | Input not flagged |
| Second-model (MUSK) agreement | Same top class | Concordant |
| Similar cases | 5 of 5 InSitu [F5] | Neighbors support InSitu |

## Tissue evidence
- **Dense lymphocytic infiltrate** (regions 0, 7, 9) · context · Above typical; descriptive, no invasive direction [F2] · Weak
- **Tumor necrosis** (regions 1, 2, 5) · ↑ invasive · Highest-scoring concept here, but spot check 3/20 · Unreliable
- **Tumor infiltrating stroma** (region 10) · ↑ invasive · Modest score; only region with high risk · Validated
- **Marked nuclear pleomorphism** (region 6) · ↓ invasive · Below-typical score; concept model links this to lower invasive likelihood · Validated

## Trust check
- **Heatmap**: Removing the top 3 regions drops the invasive logit 0.54 more than random (CI 0.47–0.60); faithful to classifier.
- **Concepts**: Concept deletion CI (−0.005 to 0.007) includes 0, so not shown to reflect classifier use; case leans on Unreliable necrosis (3/20).

## Could be wrong if
- Image is a simulated, JPEG-degraded frozen section; reliability error AUROC is only 0.69.
- Region 10 alone scores 58% invasive; whole-image invasive probability is 2%.

## Check on the slide
1. **Regions 1, 2, 5:** Confirm necrosis is real; its spot check was 3/20.
2. **Region 10:** Check for stromal infiltration; this region scores 58% invasive.
3. **Regions 1, 8:** Compare duct-confined atypia against benign glands to separate InSitu from Benign.
